text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: prod-kv-cache eviction_rate > 10% for 5m on frontend-pool-1. Pager fired to @sam_oncall :rotating_light:

sam_oncall: got the page, looking now. Anyone seen config churn on cache size or TTL?

leo_sre: jumping in. checking eviction vs hit-rate dashboards. initial read: hit rate dropped from ~92% to 63% starting ~20m ago. eviction bursts coincide with a spike in short-lived keys from a canary rollout.

maria_prod: that canary was a small feature we rolled to 5% earlier. It uses session-prefixed cache keys and might be setting 0 TTL by mistake. @jordan_support saw errors?

jordan_support: customer reports increased latencies -> a few 503 fallbacks from Reranker. Not widespread, approx 2% of requests from the affected region.

sam_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) disable canary traffic to frontend-pool-1 via routing rule rollback, 2) temporarily raise cache capacity for frontend-pool-1, 3) mute noisy eviction alert until we tune thresholds. Doing step 1 now.

leo_sre: step 1 done. Rolling back router rule to route canary -> fallback-pool. Confirmed traffic drop.

incident-bot: Deploy Rollback: canary-feature v3 -> rolled back by sam_oncall at 3m ago.

sam_oncall: while rollback propagates, increasing eviction alert threshold to reduce noise: currently fires at 5% sustained for 3m — bumping to 12% for 5m to avoid repeat paging while we triage. Acknowledge this is temporary; will create ticket for tuning.

maria_prod: found the bug in canary handler: session keys were set with TTL=0 in one branch. Pushing hotfix to canary code to default to 24h TTL. Patch PR: \`fix/canary-default-ttl\`

leo_sre: before merging, we should validate on staging and then re-roll the canary to a narrower user set. Also I want to add immediate cache eviction alarm: if eviction_rate spike co-occurs with hit_rate drop of >20% and increased downstream latency -> page. That should reduce noisy pages caused by transient evictions.

sam_oncall: agree. For now, rolling up quick dashboards and search queries:
```
# kql-ish
metric: cache.eviction_rate{env:prod, pool:frontend-pool-1} | timeseries(1m)
metric: cache.hit_rate{env:prod, pool:frontend-pool-1} | timeseries(1m)
trace: service:reranker latency p95{env:prod}
```

sam_oncall: pushing a temporary dashboard link: https://graf.example.com/d/kv-cache/evictions-hot?org=redwood (internal)

jordan_support: customer-impact note for ops: impacted customers (approx 12 tenants) saw median latency bump ~120ms, p95 up ~650ms, and a handful of timed-out embedding requests. Documenting on the incident page.

olivia_pm: flagging on product side. Are any SLA targets at risk? We need to notify accounts if SLA breaches likely.

maria_prod: hotfix merged to branch; will re-run canary in 15m against fallback-pool and monitor key distribution.

leo_sre: a few follow-ups for long-term: 1) add a hit-rate-by-key-prefix dashboard to detect noisy prefixes, 2) add auto-mitigation to throttle canary key writes if eviction_rate > X, 3) make eviction alerts composite with downstream latency as I suggested. I'll open infra tickets.

sam_oncall: opening incident tracker: INC-2026-045 (short-lived cache eviction storm). I'll include timelines, mitigation steps, customer impact, and post-incident action items.

incident-bot: oncall handoff scheduled: @sam_oncall -> @leo_sre in 40m. Please ack the handoff and ensure runbook updated re: eviction alerts.

sam_oncall: ack handoff. leaving notes in the runbook: "If eviction_rate spike, check recent deployments/rollouts, inspect key prefix distribution, and consider immediate routing rollback. Tune alert to composite signals to avoid noisy pages."

leo_sre: ack. I'll pick up monitoring work: adding two panels to the main infra dashboard tonight — 1) hit-rate heatmap by prefix, 2) eviction-to-latency composite alert visualization. Also adding an alert that fires a low-priority channel (eng-runtime) when eviction_rate between 6-12% so we can watch trends without paging.

maria_prod: will add unit/regression test to prevent TTL=0 regressions, plus a staging job that simulates heavy short-lived key writes to ensure eviction behavior is acceptable.

jordan_support: drafting customer comms: internal note + optional outreach to impacted enterprise customers tomorrow if INC-2026-045 shows SLA risk.

sam_oncall: closing loop on temporary alert changes: will revert threshold to more conservative values after we have the composite alert in place and dashboards validated.

leo_sre: estimated timeline: dashboards + alerts staged by EOD, composite alert in prod by tomorrow morning; tickets assigned: INFRA-1121 (hit-rate dashboard), INFRA-1122 (composite eviction alert), PROD-2209 (canary TTL regression fix).

maria_prod: re-run canary in 10m against limited pool, watching hit-rate. If hit-rate stays >85% and eviction_rate <3% for 15m, we'll re-enable original routing.

sam_oncall: note for postmortem: root cause = canary code path setting TTL=0 leading to mass short-lived write churn, causing KV cache eviction storms; secondary cause = alert threshold too low and not composite with downstream impact which led to immediate paging. Remediation: code fix, alert tuning, new dashboards, auto-throttle suggestion.

jordan_support: adding customer impact summary to incident doc and tagging accounts team.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: evictions normalized after rollback+hotfix. Pager un-fired. Duration: ~45m.

sam_oncall: thanks team. I'll draft the post-incident TL;DR and post to #incidents and #product. Assigning action owners in INC-2026-045.

leo_sre: quick retrospective note: preference for composite alerts + prefixed hit-rate panels before rolling aggressive canaries. Also recommend adding synthetic tests that exercise cache key patterns during canary runs.

maria_prod: +1. Also will add a pre-deploy lint step to catch TTL=0 semantically.

jordan_support: will prepare a customer-facing summary if needed.

olivia_pm: please loop me in on the postmortem. We need to update release checklist for canaries.

sam_oncall: will send PM + link to postmortem when ready. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
